intended_object: A (noncomputably chosen) well-order, i.e. a linear well-founded order, on α that extends a given well-founded relation r: if r a b then a < b. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation of Mathlib/Order/Extension/Well.lean.
explanation: The order is the pullback of the lexicographic order on Ordinal ×ₗ Cardinal along a ↦ (rank r a, embeddingToCardinal a). The map is injective because its second coordinate is, so LinearOrder.lift' gives a linear order on α. It extends r because r a b implies rank r a < rank r b (rank_lt_of_rel), as proved in exists_well_order_ge. It is well-founded because it is the inverse image of a lexicographic product of two well-founded orders; the instances wellOrderExtension.wellFounded_lt and isWellOrder_lt right after the definition prove this. Returning a LinearOrder and proving well-foundedness separately is standard Mathlib style. The setting, an arbitrary type with a well-founded relation, is fully general.
